docs.title: Making Forward Deployed Engineering repeatable.
docs.text:
We advise companies on how to run Forward Deployed Engineering, and we assess and train their FDEs.

Forward Deployed Engineering is not a standard org chart. Depending on the product and business model, it can be a product-discovery function, a way to deliver complex customer outcomes, or simply the wrong answer.

Platypus helps leaders make that choice. Then we help them set up the operating model, interview process and training to match.

Featured in The Pragmatic Engineer

Anjor's account of how Palantir ran Forward Deployed Engineering is featured in The Pragmatic Engineer, read by more than 500,000 engineers.

docs.text: An eight-week, remote programme that gets new FDEs ready to lead deployments. A two-day exercise on a realistic client case, six weeks of coaching on their own live work, and a written verdict on each FDE. There is a team programme for AI startups and a cohort programme for services firms. It is not a course.

docs.title: The Platypus FDE Blueprint
docs.text: The Blueprint is the framework behind our FDE work. It helps a company decide whether it needs Forward Deployed Engineers, what shape the function should take and how to tell whether it is working.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
An FDE closes the gap between what a product can do today and what a customer needs in order to get value. That role is useful only when the work teaches the company something reusable—about the product, the market or the delivery capability.

The Blueprint works through nine questions:

  1. Do you need FDEs at all? Start with the deployment problem, not the title.
  2. Where does the compounding asset live? In a product you sell, or a delivery capability you keep?
  3. How mature is the product? Product maturity determines how much autonomy the field needs.
  4. What is the smallest team that can own an outcome? Avoid separating the customer context from the ability to build.
  5. How does the field work with product, sales and steady-state delivery? The interfaces define the function.
  6. What should improve over time? Measure leverage, people required per deployment and time to customer value.
  7. Who should you hire? Test judgment, learning speed and ownership as well as technical ability.
  8. How does the model fail? Common failures include copying the title, weak product feedback and rewarding attendance rather than outcomes.
  9. What should change next? Apply the framework to the company and turn it into a small number of concrete decisions.

docs.title: Two coherent models
docs.text:
Product company Services company Compounding asset A product customers buy A delivery capability the firm keeps FDE's role Discover what the product must become Deliver better outcomes with increasing leverage Healthy direction Fewer FDEs needed as the product matures More impact delivered per FDE Main risk Custom work never becomes product Linear consulting under a new title

Both models can work. Problems begin when a company operates one while hiring, measuring or selling as though it were the other.

The FDE Readiness Assessment applies the Blueprint to one organisation. Practical templates and longer-form guidance are available in the open FDE Advisory Materials.

docs.title: The FDE Programme
docs.text:
An eight-week, remote programme that gets new FDEs ready to lead deployments. It is not a course. The AI labs teach the tools. The hard part is the craft of making a deployment work, and that grows through feedback on real work from people who have done it.

  • A two-day exercise. Each pod gets a realistic client, not a specification. We play the client, and we know the answer, so feedback is sharp and every FDE faces the same test.
  • Six weeks of coaching on real work. Each deployment team brings its live deployment to a coach for an hour a week. The coach asks who makes the call, which decision is being modelled and what changed for the user. Then they set one thing for next week.
  • A written verdict on each FDE. In week 8, each FDE defends a fresh case to a panel. The verdict is ready to lead a deployment, ready with support, or not yet, with the evidence behind it. A short check follows 90 days later.

You also get a note on what in your company is blocking your FDEs, and the exercise, rubric and coach guide, licensed for internal use.

Team programme Cohort programme For AI startups with new FDEs on live deployments and no senior FDE to coach them Services firms and deployment companies building an FDE practice Size Up to about four FDEs Up to about eight FDEs Coaches Ours Your senior people, calibrated by us, or ours Price From £48,500 From £62,000

Add-ons include a case built from one of your own solved engagements, coaching beyond week 7 by the month, and moderation of repeat cohorts you run yourselves. In-person days are available, with travel at cost.

docs.title: FDE Readiness Assessment
docs.text:
A two-week assessment for a company deciding whether to build an FDE function, or trying to understand why an existing one is not working as expected.

We review the current plan and evidence, speak to the relevant leaders and practitioners, and produce a written Readout covering:

  • what problem the field function needs to solve;
  • the most important gaps or risks;
  • our recommendation; and
  • a practical 90-day plan.

Price: £15,000.

docs.title: Operating Model + Interview System Sprint
docs.text:
A fixed three-week engagement for a company ready to design or reset the function. It produces:

  • an operating model covering team shape, ownership, interfaces and measurement;
  • a hiring playbook with role profiles, interview design and calibration; and
  • a clear description of the role for candidates, customers and the wider company.

Price: £40,000.

Longer-term implementation support is scoped after the initial engagement. It is not sold as a generic retainer before we understand the company.

docs.title: Interview design
docs.text:
If you already know the role, we can design how you interview for it, without a broader operating-model engagement.

Interview process design: from £4,000 per role. This includes the traits, interview structure, calibrated questions and a working session with the hiring team.

Interviews: £600 each. One of our calibrated interviewers runs the interview and sends written evidence within 48 hours.

We don't source or place candidates.
